zones: SS01 Equatorial maize and cassava (100%)
primary_zone: SS01 Equatorial maize and cassava
livelihood_summary: Highly productive surplus rain-fed farming with some livestock, fishing, hunting and forest products; good cross-border markets
main_crops: Maize, sorghum, groundnuts, soya, cassava, sweet potatoes, rice, vegetables; Robusta coffee as cash crop
seasonal_calendar: Two rainy seasons (Mar-Jun, Aug-Nov); land preparation Jan-Mar; planting mid-Mar to May; cereal harvest Jul-Aug and Nov-Dec
lean_season: Dry-season stocks decline from about Apr; lean season ends late Jun when green maize is eaten
flood_pattern: River and stream floods Aug-Oct, about every 4 years; seasonal flooding makes some roads impassable in the rains
main_hazards: Dry spells May-Jul (about every 2 years); river and stream floods Aug-Oct (about every 4 years); crop pests every rainy season; conflict and insecurity
wealth_determinants: Land cultivated (poor about 0.8 ha, hand tools; better-off 2-4 ha with hired labor and tractors), crop types grown in both seasons, productive assets
markets_and_trade: Border markets Nabiapai and Bazi (DRC, Kenya, Uganda); Yambio, Yei, Ikotos, Nimule, Namaku, Koliko; surplus maize sold to traders and WFP (P4P); roads to Juba; several currencies in use
consumption_calendar_poor: Own crops normally last poor households about 9 months (Jul-Mar), now 4-7 months; market purchase of maize, sorghum and other foods for remaining months; wild food consumption peaks in rains; better-off largely self-sufficient
income_and_expenditure: Poor: bush product sales, labor, brewing; better-off: food and cash crop (coffee) sales, retail trade; livestock sales peak in dry season
access_constraints: Poor road maintenance and seasonal flooding make some roads impassable in the rains; insecurity; long distances; inflation; displacement to Uganda and IDP camps
coping_and_notes: Wild foods, bush product and charcoal sales, labor migration, remittances, livestock sales
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018; zone shares from FEWS NET 2018 shapefile overlaid on county boundaries

zones: SS04 Western plains groundnuts sesame and sorghum (100%)
primary_zone: SS04 Western plains groundnuts sesame and sorghum
livelihood_summary: Subsistence rain-fed farming with forest products, seasonal fishing and small livestock; formerly a surplus area
main_crops: Groundnuts and sesame (cash), sorghum, maize, cassava, cowpeas, pumpkins, vegetables
seasonal_calendar: Rainy season Apr-Oct; land preparation Feb-Apr; planting May to mid-Jun; weeding mid-Jun to Jul; green harvest from Sep; sorghum and sesame harvested in March
lean_season: Not stated; green harvest from Sep, sorghum and sesame harvested in Mar
flood_pattern: Seasonal flooding limits market access; floods along rivers and low-lying areas are periodic
main_hazards: Dry spells and late season start about every 2 years (May-Jun); crop pests Jun-Dec; livestock disease; cross-border conflict; price spikes
wealth_determinants: Land size, farming tools and labor (poor hand tools, short of labor; better-off ox-plows, bicycles, timber and bamboo)
markets_and_trade: Raja, Aroyo, Kuarjena, Mapel, Kangi, Bar Mayen, Aweil, Namatina, Duma, Nagero; Wau; South Darfur (Sudan)
consumption_calendar_poor: Own cereal normally 9 months (Sep-May), now 4-6 months; poor buy sorghum Jun-Aug with few income sources in those months; cassava year-round and in-kind labor cushion shortfalls
income_and_expenditure: Poor: groundnut sales, natural products (charcoal, bamboo, honey, shea); better-off: groundnut, sesame, cassava, sorghum, tobacco, timber; school fees Mar-Apr
access_constraints: Seasonal flooding and poor roads; LRA insecurity in neighboring CAR; staple prices up 6-10 times at Wau market since 2016 while labor wages rose 2 times
coping_and_notes: Groundnut sales; natural product sales (charcoal, grass, bamboo, honey, shea); sorghum in-kind labor
